title.narrative: World Cities Report 2022: Envisaging the Future of Cities

description.narrative:
In 2013, an evaluation of the existing flagship reports (the Global Report on Human Settlements and the State of the World’s Cities Report) recommended the merger of the two reports into a single flagship report for UN-Habitat. This decision was generally welcomed by external audiences. It also presented an opportunity to change the methods and process of report production and dissemination, and to significantly strengthen modes of information-sharing, communication, and integration of UN-Habitat’s normative and operational work. The outcome of this process was the conceptualization of the World Cities Report as UN-Habitat’s flagship report. The first edition of this Report and its abridged version was published in 2016—World Cities Report 2016: Urbanization and Development—Emerging Urban Futures. The second edition and its abridged version—World Cities Report 2020: The Value of Sustainable Urbanization—was published in 2020.
The purpose of the project is to publish the third issue of the World Cities Report. This project document covers the activities related to the production of the World Cities Report 2022 (WCR 2022) which will be published in June 2022. The theme of the Report is: Envisaging the Future of Cities. It comes at a time when various stakeholders are concerned with the future of cities following the devastating impacts of COVID-19 on urban areas across the world. Indeed, cities remain central to the sustainable development trajectory and as such, their futures should be inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable, as called for by Goal 11 of the SDGs. These futures should also be compatible with the transformative commitments of the New Urban Agenda to ensure that no one is left behind, by being people-centered and socially inclusive; creating inclusive prosperity and opportunities for all; and being environmentally sustainable. Based on the lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic, urban futures should create resilient cities, with the “ability to absorb, recover and prepare for future shocks (economic, environmental, social and institutional, while at the same time promoting sustainable development, well-being and inclusive growth.”
The WCR 2022 seeks to provide greater insights and clarity on the future of cities based on existing trends, challenges and opportunities. In the current setting, these will include the disruptive conditions emanating from the current pandemic and the valuable lessons cities are learning from it, and suggest ways cities can be better prepared to address future pandemics and a wide range of other shocks. As with the previous UN-Habitat flagship reports, the WCR 2022 will play a key role in UN-Habitat’s monitoring and reporting on urban conditions and trends both globally, regionally and at country level—an essential element to both reporting progress on the SDG 11 and as well as providing evidence-based information to build sustainable urban policies at every level of urban governance as envisaged by UN-Habitat’s Strategic Plan 2020-2023. This Report will synthesize information and knowledge on the state of cities and human settlements with a view to strengthen the ability of key partners, stakeholders and governments at all levels to use such information to formulate and implement effective urban policies that will realize sustainable urban futures as encapsulated by the SDGs and the NUA.
